Organic Chemistry I¶

Key Norms by A. G. Hossion¶

Lesson-01, 02, 03.¶

Lesson-01_ch01&02¶

⏣ How to read and/or draw bond line and condensed structure of Organic compounds, Functional Groups (FG)¶

  • Bond-Line Drawings : How to read and draw Bond-Line/Condensed structure Drawings?
  • FG: Identification and naming Functional groups of organic compounds - alkane, alkene, alkyne, alkyl halide, alcohol, ether, thiol, aromatic or arene, ketone, aldehyde, carboxylic acid, acyl halide, anhydride, ester, amide and amine.

Lesson-02_ch01¶

⏣ Hybrid Atomic Orbitals (AOs), Molecular Orbitals (MOs)¶

  • Hybrid atomic orbitals: Know sp, sp2, sp3 hybrid orbitals. Understand how sigma bond, pi bond, carbon-carbon double bond, carbon-carbon triple bond are form. Know unshared pairs of electron hybridization for oxygen and nitrogen containing compounds. and Steric number.

Lesson-03_ch01¶

⏣ Polar and non-Polar Compounds, Dipole moment(µ)¶

  • Polar and non-polar covalent bond : Know the difference covalent bond vs polar covalent bond. Get familiar to identify partial charges vs complete charges.
  • Dipole moment: What is dipole moment(µ)? Learn how to calculate and draw dipole moment (sign) for a bond (C-Cl, etc) in compounds. Predict molecular geometry on the basis of VSEPR theory. Know how to identify whether compound can exhibit dipole moment and compound is polar or non-polar.
  • Intermolecular forces and physical properties - m.p., b.p., solubility: What are dipole-dipole interaction, hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces and/or fleeting dipole-dipole interactions? And understand how these properties change the physical properties of melting point/ boiling point/ Solubility of compounds. Protic/aprotic solvent.

🍓🍓Concept Check and/or Mastering the Modality¶

    H2O , CH4O

  • which of the following protic and aprotic solvent, explain:

Lesson-04¶

Lesson-04_ch02¶

⏣ Resoanace structure and Curved arrow drawing¶

  • Formal Charge : Understand how to identify formal charges in the structure. Know how to calculate formal charges of atoms in the structure.
  • Formal charge on Carbon: Carbon atoms with formal charges, know Carbocation Vs Carboanion and understand how to identify lone pairs on oxygen and nitrogen atoms.
  • Curved arrow and resonance structure: understand the five patterns, how to draw right arrow to valid correct resonance structure. (i) Formal charges in resonance structure - allylic (ii) Drawing resonance structure via pattern recognition
  • What is resonance hybrid and understand delocalized and localized lone pairs.

Lesson-05¶

Lesson-05_ch03¶

⏣ Acids and Bases¶

  • Acids and Bases: Know acids and bases definition on the basis of Bronsted-Lowry concept and Lewis concept. Understand how to compare the strength of acids and bases on the basis of structure of molecules (in absence of pKa or pKb values).
  • Lewis Acids and Bases: Be able to justify Lewis concept is the most fundamental of the acid-base concepts, and the most general; it includes all the other concepts such as Bronsted-Lowry concept. Lewis concept of acidity and basicity fundamental to our understanding of Organic Chemistry.
  • Curved arrow and electron density: Know how to draw curved arrow to show the flow of electron density and transferring proton.
  • Acidity on the basis of Bronsted-Lowry and Lewis Acids-Bases Concepts:

    Quantitative Perspective: [pKa and proton transfer ability] Understand how to use pKa to compare acidity and basicity.
    Qualitative Perspective: Be able to understand the factors such as charge on atoms, resonance, induction, sp/sp2/sp3 orbitals affect the stability of conjugate base. Understand how to compare the strength of acids and bases on the basis of structure of molecules (in absence of pKa or pKb values).
    Be able to use both qualitative and quantitative perspectives to predict the position of equilibrium in reaction. Organic acid-base mechanism.

  • Leveling and solvent effects and counter-ions: Understand the strongest base and the strongest acid can be present in any particular solvent such as in a basic solution and/or in an acidic solution.

Lesson-06, 07¶

Lesson-06_ch04¶

⏣ Alkane (open chain hydrocarbon, saturated hydrocarbon CnH2n+2)¶

  • IUPAC Naming alkane: Know how to name saturated hydrocarbon, alkane (both open chain and cyclic).
  • Isomerism: How to draw constitutional isomers of small molecule.
  • Constitutional isomers: Know constitutional isomers of alkane and stability of alkanes.
  • Newman projection formula: Understand how to draw Newman projection formula. Know how to rotate carbon- carbon single bond and understand conformations (eclipsed vs staggered conformations) and torisional strain of saturated hydrocarbon. Be able to identify and compare highest and lowest conformations from structure of molecule.

🍓🍓Concept Check and/or Mastering the Modality¶

  • Identify whether the following (two pairs) drawings represent constitutional isomers or whether they are simply different representations of the same compound. Identify which drawing has the highest parent chain and IUPAC name each drawing.

    Or draw the line structure from IUPAC naming.


2,2,4-Trimethylpentane

  • Draw each of the following compounds as a bond-line structure, and then assign IUPAC names for each. Or, assign IUPAC names for each and then Draw a Newman projection of the following compound as viewed from the angle indicated, draw staggered, eclipsed, gauche or anti-gauche (if any) and identy most stable (less energy) vs least stable (high energy).

Lesson-07_ch04¶

⏣ Cycloalkane (ring-closed chain/bicyclic, saturated cycloalkane CnH2n)¶

  • Naming cycloalkane: Know the structure of cycloalkane such as single ring cycloalkane general formula CnH2n and how to name cycloalkane and bicyclic alkane (both open chain and cyclic).
  • Cycloalkane stability: Understand stability of cycloalkane and how to draw conformation of cyclohexane including axial, equatorial, chair and boat transformation.
  • Geometrical/Stereoisomerism: cis- and trans-

Lesson-08, 09¶

Lesson-08(ch-05)¶

⏣ Stereoisomerism - Enantiomers, Optical Activity¶

  • ***cis- & *trans-** : Understand how to draw and identify isomer (cis-, and trans-) and stereoisomer.
  • Chirality: Be able to identify chirality center, chiral molecule, achiral molecule, enantiomers.
  • Optically active: know how experimentally optical activity can be determined. know specific rotation, dextrorotatory and + sign, levorotatory and - sign.
  • Enantiomers:Be able to draw and identify enantiomers.

Understand what is racemic modification, enantiometric excess (ee) and be able to calculate optical purity from given enantiomeric data.

Understand how to identify and configure R- and S- configuration. be able to use R-, S- configuration in IUPAC
nomenclature.

🍓🍓Concept Check and/or Mastering the Modality¶

, CH3CH(Cl)CH(Cl)CH3, CH3CH(Cl)CH(Cl)CHH2-OH

This solution was then placed in a sample cell with a pathlength of 10.0 cm and the observed rotation was +0.78°. Calculate the %ee of the mixture.
  • 2-butanol that contains 75% ()-2-butanol and 25% ()-2-butanol, Calculate the %ee of the mixture.

⏣ Stereoisomerism - Diastreomers, meso compounds, optical inactive¶

  • Optically active vs inactive:Understand how to identify and distinguish enantiomers, diastereomers and Meso compound. know why enantiomer and meso compound are optically inactive., and diastereomers is optically active.
  • ***E- & *Z-**: Know E- and Z- Designations Vs cis- and trans-.

Know the resolution of enantiomers.

Lesson-10(ch-06)¶

⏣ Curved arrow, Nucleophile/Electrophile, Carbocation rearrangement¶

  • Curved arrow Understand how to draw pushing arrow (curved arrow) , loss of a leaving group, proton transfers.
  • Nucleophiles-Electrophiles: Be able to identify Nucleophile vs Electrophiles.
  • Nucleophile-Base: Be able to distinguish Nucleophile vs Base.
  • Carbocation rearrangement: Know how to rearrange carbocation and the stability of carbocation such as primary, secondary and tertiary.
  • Reversible-Ireeversible reaction:Understand reversible Vs irreversible reactions.
